artifacts.summary: Root-causes the revert incident to an ad hoc bare git-snapshot.sh call in task 186's plan, documents file_scope's shape/reliability as the scope oracle, and recommends a runtime out-of-scope guard plus a planner-agent.md guardrail and stash-identity fix.

memory_candidates.content: state.json's file_scope field mixes three shapes across live tasks: exact file paths, directory prefixes with a trailing slash, and shell-glob patterns (e.g. 'agent-system/extensions/*/agents/**'). Any code comparing a path against file_scope must use prefix/glob matching (bash `[[ "$path" == $pattern ]]`), not exact string equality, and must have an explicit fallback for the ~10% of tasks with no file_scope declared at all.

git-snapshot.sh's default and --branch modes both revert the working tree (stash-push or commit-then-checkout); only --no-revert leaves it dirty. The only known unsafe caller pattern found in this codebase is a plan-authored 'snapshot before any edits' step using bare default mode -- no template or agent contract instructs this; it was an ad hoc habit generalized from recovery.md's rung (c) (genuine-rollback precursor) without registering that rung (c) presupposes an imminent destructive op, not a routine precaution. Every correct caller (general-implementation-agent.md, general-research-agent.md) already uses --no-revert for checkpoint-style calls.
